rows.title: Introduction to Administration of Justice
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
outcomes: Learning Outcomes
Explain the process of adjudication.
Critically analyze and discuss issues of crime and justice from varying perspectives.
Describe theories of criminology used to explain crime and criminality.
Explain the definitions of crime.
Explain the methods, theories, and concepts associated with the sources of crime data, the emerging patterns of criminal activity, and the costs of crime.
Identify and describe special issues in the criminal justice system involving juvenile delinquency, drugs, and the future development.
Explain the history and function of corrections and law enforcement in the United States, including police, probation, parole, community corrections, prisons and jails.
Analyze crime data in the United States.
Apply theories of criminology to create informed positions on controversial issues in criminal justice.

rows.title: Introduction To Animal Science
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
outcomes: Learning Outcomes
Collect and evaluate data used to ensure scientifically based management decisions.
Describe economically significant beef cattle, sheep, and swine breeds and identify current local, national and global animal husbandry practices.
Explain animal behavior as it relates to the animal's health and performance.
Identify animal contributions to human needs and discuss issues affecting consumer and producer awareness of animal welfare, food safety and the environment.
Evaluate livestock body conformation, life cycles and biotechnological principles of animal production for basic nutritional needs and feeding practices.

rows.title: Introduction to Plant Science
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
outcomes: Learning Outcomes
Categorize the biological competitors of higher plants.
Categorize the roles of higher plants in the living world.
Define sexual and asexual reproduction in higher plants.
Define the climatic influences on plant growth and development.
Define the physical and chemical properties of soils and soil erosion problems.
Explain the scientific method and its application in solving problems in plant and soil science.
Explain photosynthesis, respiration, and translocation in higher plants.
Explain the standard plant propagation methods.

rows.title: Survey of Art from Prehistory to the Medieval Era
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
outcomes: Learning Outcomes
Identify, examine, and assess representative works of art and architecture from prehistoryto the medieval era employing appropriate art historical terminology.
Develop critical thinking, information literacy, and problem-solving through an engagement with art, architecture, artists, and patrons from prehistory to the medieval era.
2.Analyze works of art and architecture in terms of aesthetic, socio-political, religious,historical, technological, and cultural contexts in which they were created.

rows.title: General Chemistry I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
outcomes: Learning Outcomes
Apply chemical principles to specific chemical processes.
Describe major chemical concepts, theoretical principles and experimental findings in chemistry as outlined in the course topics.
Develop laboratory skills by correctly assembling, executing, and employing standard laboratory techniques such as titration.
Interpret, calculate and reach logical conclusions of experimental results after reviewing experimental outcomes through direct observation and data collection.
Master mathematical techniques by employing critical thinking skills to solve chemistry word problems.
Read and communicate effectively various chemical concepts, theories, laws and experimental findings.

rows.title: Observation and Assessment
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
outcomes: Learning Outcomes
Develop recommendations and identify teaching strategies for planning, curriculum, interactions, and the environment based on observations and assessments.
Differentiate between various observation and assessment tools according to their purpose and validity.
Demonstrate basic formative and summative assessment techniques.
Apply knowledge of development and other influencing factors to interpret observations and assessments.
Use standardized observation and assessment tools to evaluate quality in environments, interactions, and curriculum.
Discuss logistical challenges, biases, and preconceptions about observing and assessing children.
Demonstrate how observation and assessment are used to plan for and adjust learning experiences.
Describe legal and ethical responsibilities in relation to observation, assessment, documentation, and recordkeeping.
Discuss the role of partnerships with families and other professionals in utilizing interpretations of observational and assessment data.

rows.title: Emergency Medical Technician - Basic
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
outcomes: Learning Outcomes
Describe the roles of EMS in the health care system.
Demonstrate the professional attributes expected of EMTs.
Perform the roles and responsibilities of an EMT with regard to personal safety and wellness, as well as the safety of others.
Perform the duties of an EMT with regard for medical-legal and ethical issues, including functioning under medical direction and within the scope of practice.
Apply principles of anatomy, physiology, pathophysiology, life span development, and therapeutic communication to the assessment and management of patients.
Identify the need for and perform immediate lifesaving interventions to manage a patient's airway, breathing, and circulation.
Assess and manage patients of all ages with a variety of complaints, medical conditions, and traumatic injuries.

Apply principles of emergency medical services operations, including considerations in ambulance and air medical transportation, multiple-casualty incidents, gaining access to and extricating patients, hazardous materials incidents, and responding to situations involving weapons of mass destruction.

rows.title: Native American Studies
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
outcomes: Learning Outcomes

Describe and compare the relationships and impact of Indian individuals, communities, nations, confederacies prior to and throughout the European colonial period by examining and applying skills learned in analyzing original, oral, primary, secondary, and tertiary sources.

Apply theory and knowledge produced by Native American communities to describe the critical events, histories, cultures, contributions, lived experiences, and struggles of those groups with a particular emphasis on agency and identity.

Analyze the intersection of race and racism as they relate to class, gender, sexuality, religion, tribal citizenship, sovereignty, language, and/or age in Native American communities in the context of federal legislation and policies.

Analyze and articulate concepts such as race and racism, racialization, ethnicity, equity, white supremacy, self-determination, decolonization, sovereignty, imperialism, settler colonialism, and anti-racism as analyzed in Native American studies.

rows.title: Weight Training
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
outcomes: Learning Outcomes
Correctly demonstrate spotting techniques.
Demonstrate how to perform each exercise with proper technique and identify the muscle groups used.
Demonstrate proper techniques when performing various weight lifting exercises.

rows.title: Keyboarding I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
outcomes: Learning Outcomes
Increase rate of speed and accuracy of words per minute
Key at 35 words per minute for 3minutes with 3 or fewer errors by the end of the course

rows.title: Intravenous Therapy/Blood Withdrawal
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
outcomes: Learning Outcomes
Define the terminology related to infusion-related professional practice
Perform successful venipunctures on at least 3 live human subjects
Demonstrate universal precautions
Describe potential complications of intravenous therapy and blood withdrawal
Demonstrate safety precautions utilized to prevent complications
Identify nursing diagnoses and interventions related to fluid and electrolyte balance
Compare the advantages and disadvantages of various parenteral fluids
Successfully document care of the client while performing venipuncture and assessment of client with ongoing intravenous and blood transfusion therapy

rows.title: Introduction To Astronomy
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
outcomes: Learning Outcomes
Students will be able to explain in general terms the evolution and life cycles of stars, galaxies and, more speculatively, our universe.
Students will be able to trace how the history of astronomical observations and ideas have influenced the history of humankind and our cognition of our place in the world and universe.

Students will demonstrate an understanding a number of different classes of objects visible in our cosmic landscape by explaining some of their properties, scales and how we have been able to use scientific models to explain what these objects are.
